summary: Ernest Francisco Fenollosa worked in philosophy, Japanology, and art history. He studied at Harvard and the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston, later teaching at the University of Tokyo (1878) and curating at the Boston Museum of Fine Arts (1890–1896).

Ernest John Henry Mackay was a scholar of archaeology and Indology. Educated at the University of Bristol, he served as Custodian of Antiquities in Mandatory Palestine (1919–1922) and Special Officer for Exploration with the Archaeological Survey of India (~1926–1931).

Ernest Renan was a French scholar of religious studies, history, and linguistics. He studied under Eugène Burnouf and Etienne Marc Quatremère, later holding posts at the Bibliothèque nationale de France (1851–1860) and the Collège de France from 1861.

Ernest Sosa is an American philosopher. He studied at the University of Miami and the University of Pittsburgh under Roderick M. Chisholm. Sosa held major professorial posts at Brown University from 1964 and Rutgers University (1998–2006).

Ernst Curtius was a German archaeologist and historian. He studied under Karl Otfried Müller, August Boeckh, and Friedrich Gottlieb Welcker, later serving as professor at the University of Göttingen (1855–1867), the University of Berlin (1844, 1863, 1867), and directing the Altes Museum (~1872–1896).

Ernst Förstemann was a German linguist and historian. Mentored by August Friedrich Pott, Karl Lachmann, and Franz Bopp, he studied at Berlin and Halle, later working as a librarian at Wernigerode (1851) and head of the Dresden Library (1865–1887).

Ernst Fürlinger is a scholar of religious studies and Indology who completed his habilitation at the University of Vienna. His career includes posts at St. Virgil Salzburg (1991–2001), the University of Vienna (2006–2016), and the University for Continuing Education Krems (2007–).

Ernst Haas was a German Indologist who studied at the universities of Bonn, Berlin (under Albrecht Weber), and Tübingen. He held posts at the British Museum (1866) and served as Professor of Sanskrit at University College London from 1875.

Ernst Johann Eitel was a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies. He earned his MA and PhD at the University of Tübingen and later served as professor of German language and literature at the University of Adelaide (~1897–1908).

Ernst Kuhn was a German Indologist and linguist who studied under Albrecht Weber and Rudolf von Roth at Berlin, Leipzig, Tübingen, and Halle. He held professorships at the University of Heidelberg (1875) and the University of Munich (1877–1917).

Ernst Leumann was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied under Albrecht Weber and completed doctorates at Leipzig and Strasbourg. He worked on the Sanskrit-English Dictionary at Oxford (1882–1884) and held professorships at Strasbourg (from 1884) and Freiburg (1919).

Ernst Moritz Arndt was a German historian. He completed his studies at the universities of Greifswald and Jena, and subsequently held academic posts at the University of Greifswald (~1800–1811) and the University of Bonn (~1818–1860).

Ernst Osiander was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied under Rudolf von Roth at the University of Tübingen (1847–1853), later serving as a Repetent at Maulbronn and Blaubeuren (~1852–1854) and the Tübinger Stift (1857–1860).

Ernst Steinkellner is an Austrian scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology who studied under Erich Frauwallner. He served as director at the University of Vienna (1973–2006) and the Institute for Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia (1998–2006).

Ernst Trumpp was a scholar of linguistics, Indology, and religious studies. He studied under Rudolf von Roth at the Tübinger Stift, later serving at the East India Company (~1850–1854), Tübingen (1871), and as professor at the University of Munich (1874).

Ernst Waldschmidt worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Central Asian studies. He studied under Paul Deussen, Emil Sieg, Heinrich Lüders, and others at Kiel, Göttingen, and Berlin. He held the chair of Indology at the University of Göttingen (1936–1965).

Ernst Windisch was a German Indologist and linguist who studied under Georg Curtius, Friedrich Ritschl, and Hermann Brockhaus at Leipzig. He held chairs of comparative linguistics at Heidelberg (1872) and Strasbourg (1875) before returning to Leipzig in 1877.

Ernst Zinn was a German scholar in linguistics and classics. He held academic posts at Saarland University (1951–1956), the University of Hamburg (~1951–1957), and the University of Tübingen (~1957–1978).

Erwin Rousselle was a Sinologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Friedrich Krause, Max Walleser, and Alexander von Staël-Holstein. He held posts at Peking University (1924–1929), Yenching University, Frankfurt University (1935), and directed the China-Institut Frankfurt.
Esben Andreasen is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. He studied at the University of Copenhagen and served as a visiting researcher at Otani University in 1992.
